# Patches to vendored crates

Baseline for each crate is the upstream commit in `UPSTREAM.txt`. Every deviation is listed here with the reason.

## ssh_agent

The socket-path rows are `#[cfg(unix)]` and purely additive: the upstream entry points and their tests are untouched. The `protocol.rs` row fixes behavior; the `clear` row is an additive public entry point.

| File | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/server/listener/unix.rs` | `UnixListener::bind(PathBuf)` holds the old body of `new()`; `new()` now calls it with `get_socket_path()`. | Lets the caller choose the socket path without mutating the process-wide `BITWARDEN_SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. |
| `src/server/listener/mod.rs` | New `create_listeners_at(PathBuf)`. | Plumbing for the path. |
| `src/server/mod.rs` | New `SSHAgentServer::start_at_socket_path(PathBuf)`. | Plumbing for the path. |
| `src/agent.rs` | New public `BitwardenSSHAgent::start_at(PathBuf)`. | Entry point used by `crates/ssh`. |
| `src/server/protocol.rs` | `detect_namespace` reads the namespace right after the 6-byte `SSHSIG` magic instead of after magic + a `u32` version. Its unit-test helper `make_sshsig_blob` drops the version field, `detect_namespace_truncated_after_version_returns_unsupported` becomes `..._after_magic_...` with the same intent, and `detect_namespace_reads_the_layout_openssh_signs` is new. | Upstream bug, not Unix-specific: the data an agent signs for `ssh-keygen -Y sign` is `SSHSIG`, namespace, reserved, hash algorithm, hash (`sshsig_wrap_sign` in OpenSSH); the version only exists in the armored signature. With the old offset every real `git`/`file` signature was reported as `Unsupported`, so the approval UI never saw the namespace. Observed with OpenSSH 10.5 in `crates/ssh/tests/agent.rs`. |
| `src/agent.rs` | New public `BitwardenSSHAgent::clear()` calling `KeyStore::clear()` (which resets `initialized`), plus the unit test `clear_clears_the_keystore_without_stopping`. | Upstream only clears on `stop()`, and `replace(vec![])` leaves the keystore `initialized`, so after the first key refresh a list request never reaches `request_list_approval`. vaultkeeper clears on lock / log out / account switch so a locked vault serves no keys and `ssh-add -l` asks the user to unlock. |
| `src/server/listener/windows.rs` | The named pipe is created with `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`, `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` and ends with the DACL `D:P(A;;0x12019b;;;<user sid>)(A;;RC;;;OW)`. A pool of 4 instances is created up front with `WRITE_DAC` from the setup DACL `D:P(A;;0x14019f;;;<user sid>)` (the final one denies us `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE` and the owner ACE strips `WRITE_DAC`), the final DACL is applied to every instance with `SetKernelObjectSecurity`, and each instance is recycled after its client disconnects (the recycle first waits up to 2 s for the client to close its end, because `DisconnectNamedPipe` discards data the client has not read yet; then, after `DisconnectNamedPipe`, it clears the stale read/write slot state that mio keeps across `disconnect` — a settle read on the disconnected pipe, a first poll of `connect` so `ConnectNamedPipe` is in flight, and one read that consumes the leftover error — because otherwise the next client's first read receives the previous client's `ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE`/`ERROR_PIPE_NOT_CONNECTED`). Every idle instance waits for a client in its own spawned task that hands the connected instance to `accept` through a channel (Windows attaches a client to any listening instance, so awaiting one popped instance left `accept` hanging); dropping the listener aborts those tasks. New `BitwardenSSHAgent::start_on(&str)` (via `SSHAgentServer::start_on_pipe`, `create_listeners_on`) starts the agent on a given pipe name; the 21 `server_windows.rs` tests use a unique name each, with a client open that asks only for the rights the DACL grants (tokio's `ClientOptions` asks for `GENERIC_WRITE`, which is refused), and the new `ssh_add_windows.rs` runs the runner's real `ssh-add.exe -l` against an empty agent. `Win32_Storage_FileSystem` is added to the `windows` features for the test client open. A name that is already taken returns "The Windows OpenSSH Authentication Agent service is running; stop and disable it, or turn off Vaultkeeper's SSH agent". The two tests that created the pipe name twice now go through the listener. `WindowsListener::with_name` lets tests bind to a unique pipe name so they don't collide with the runner's OpenSSH agent service on `PIPE_NAME`. `Cargo.toml` adds `windows` features `Win32_Security`, `Win32_Security_Authorization`, `Win32_System_Threading`. | Upstream creates unrestricted instances on demand, so a same-user process (or the OpenSSH agent service) can squat the name or add an instance and steal the next client. The DACL withholds `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE`, which is why instances are pooled and reused. |
